{{Short description|American cryptographer (born 1955)}}
'''Gregory G. "Greg" Rose''' (born July 15, 1955, in [[Sydney|Sydney, Australia]]) was a senior vice president of technology for [[Qualcomm]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/news/technology/chair-honours-unix-veteran/2005/11/24/1132703300871.html|title=Chair honours UNIX veteran|date=November 24, 2005|work=[[Sydney Morning Herald]]|accessdate=May 20, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Sturdevant|first=Cameron |date=March 6, 2006 |title=Give Secure Code a Chance; Architecture-level views, automation and outsourcing are key |journal=eWeek|volume=23 |issue=10 |pages=35–36 |id={{ProQuest|198567722}} }}</ref> 

Rose is noted for designing the [[SOBER]] family of [[stream cipher]]s for wireless telephony.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Fast Software Encryption: 6th International Workshop, FSE'99 Rome, Italy, March 24-26, 1999 Proceedings|last=Knudsen|first=Lars|date=2003|publisher=Springer|isbn=354066226X|location=Berlin|pages=305}}</ref> Together with Philip Hawkes, he also designed [[Turing (cipher)|Turing]], a cipher system based on the SOBER-t32.<ref>{{Cite book|title=New Stream Cipher Designs: The ESTREAM Finalists|last=Robshaw|first=Matthew|last2=Billet|first2=Olivier|date=2008|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9783540683506|location=Berlin|pages=58}}</ref> It was developed to address encryption issues, particularly the limitations to processing power, program space, and memory present in software encryption algorithms.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Fast Software Encryption: 10th International Workshop, FSE 2003, LUND, Sweden, February 24-26, 2003, Revised Papers|last=Johansson|first=Thomas|date=2003|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=3540204490|location=Berlin|pages=290}}</ref>
